paper_name: Exact schedulability test for sporadic mixed-criticality real-time systems using antichains and oracles
paper_description: Models MC sporadic tasks as automaton for exact uniprocessor schedulability test using antichains and oracles to prune state space, achieving 99.998% reduction, and derives new dynamic-priority scheduler.

formal_description.statement: System as finite automaton A: states (pending jobs, mode, time mod LCM), transitions on releases/completions under scheduler sigma.

steps: State: jobs pending, HI/LO mode, phase

formal_description.statement: Antichain: incomparable states under simulation relation ~, bounding frontier in state space.
Oracle O: function pruning states s if O(s) indicates no miss possible from s.
formal_description.conclusion: Plugs in RT results for efficiency

informal_sketch.intuition: Heuristics from lit to skip safe states.

formal_description.statement: System schedulable iff no miss in antichain exploration up to bound, with oracles preserving exactness.
